The World Is Yours”  wasn’t just a song—it was a blueprint for my life. Growing up, I didn’t learn the most from textbooks; I learned from rappers who spoke about ambition, struggle, and self-determination. For anyone out there feeling the pressure: don’t let it crush you. Use it as fuel, and remember—the world is yours.

Back in 2017 I listened to this song literally hundreds of times, grinding every free hour of every day for years at that point, trying to find a way to escape my soul crushing corporate job. I moved half way around the world away from friends and family just to focus. I was so damn stressed out for years...self-doubt, tears, no one taking me seriously, financial worry everyday, loneliness, sleep-deprived, missing out on memories with loved ones back home... just exhausted.

Fast forward to mid 2019, I ended up getting laid off from that soul crushing corporate job (blessing in disguise). So I decided to go all in on my side hustle and just a few months later, the damn global pandemic happened. I was stressed AF. But I honestly didn't have it in me to slap on my happy face and start job interviewing again. I was maxing out all of my credit cards & emptied my savings. Throw in some health scares , deaths of loved ones, among other personal things, and I was at yet another low point in life. 

Fast forward to 2022, I have a growing business that generates way more income than my corporate job, I have the freedom to travel & work from anywhere in the world, earn money in my sleep on autopilot, in the best shape of my life, train muay thai & jiujitsu almost everyday, go on grand adventures, and spend quality time with family and a select group of friends. This year alone I've been to 8 countries and crossed off multiple items from my bucket list. I'm just so damn grateful. Goals can be a mirage because they constantly evolve as we do so. Sometimes we forget to pat ourselves on the back once in a while. I guess writing this right now is a bit of a pat on the back. Don't stop pursuing your dreams, but don't forget to cut yourself some slack along the way as it doesn't go exactly as planned -- it rarely does.

I'm at a place now where I'm ready to level up again... I still listen to this song on repeat - now envisioning even greater goals, and hope that I'll eventually come back to this comment thread to write about more blessings, trials, and tribulations that this song has pulled me through. Until then, GET AFTER IT.

The worst experience of my life was in 2019 at the age of 17, which left me too scared to leave my house for a month. I left school and enrolled in an alternative learning program for a while before eventually giving up and I stopped attending.  
Things did not get better during 2020 with the lock-downs. I ended up staying inside for 3 months straight... I only realized this because I decided to go for a walk one day and noticed a few changes in my mental state. The copious amounts of acid I took had messed up my mind pretty bad and left me with an eating disorder, that was only made worse by the mental problems similar to what everyone was going through during 2020. 
Stepped on the scale one day and saw that I weighed only 87 pounds at the age of 18. 
It was then that I realized that I needed to get my shit together or I was going to die from starvation. 
The first thing I did after that was make myself a sandwich, it was almost as if seeing myself get to that point was enough for me to finally turn IT ALL around. I had absolutely nothing to show for my life... luckily I had a loving family who supported me.  I was too afraid to tell them what I was going through, but they could obviously see it and always gave me hints that felt more like hurtful jabs at the time.   
Eventually, with their motivation, I got my GED by the end of 2020. Then got my first job at a car wash where I worked for a whole year.  Found myself a girlfriend and finally had enough money to pay for car insurance on my dad's old Acura. 
Fast forward 4 years, I'm top of my class in an HVACR Trade School Program and have years of experience working valet jobs in Beverly Hills, West Hollywood and Pasadena where I got to drive some of the most expensive vehicles in the world! I'm coming up on four years with my girl and I just reached 142 pounds the other day. 
After all I've been through, I found this song a few weeks ago and I bump this jam almost everyday! 
All it really takes is Patience.

video_title: Travis Scott - I KNOW ? (Official Music Video)
text: Why does no one talk about the plot of this MV? It literally showcases Travis' personal life. Here, Kylie Jenner is portrayed by Emily Ratajkowski, and, I suppose, SZA or possibly another love interest is represented by Anok Yai. From some Internet sources, I found out that he used to celebrate his birthday with Kylie on April 30th, which perfectly matches with the start of her gestational period as Stormi was born on February 1st and Aire was born on February 2nd. But then, certain problems occur in their relationship, leading him to start a new one while still missing her. Because of this, Travis spends his birthday with his new girlfriend, who eventually will stay by his side. The final scene illustrates his attempt to reconnect with Kylie, but it proves difficult as they now live in separate worlds(different interests/surroundings/cities). The directors - Dave and Travis, did a good job indeed!

Sincerely,
T.B. Wick

text: HAPPY 10th ANNIVERSARY TO LIFESTYLE. I really can't process or believe that this song is 10 years old. This was on the radio everywhere in 2014. You couldn't go an hour without hearing this song. This was my and my cousins' song and we still listen to it. I was only 5 when this song came out and I'm from Jersey. The first time I heard this song was in June or July 2014. I heard this when my dad and I were having a father and son day out and we headed to New York City on a train to head to the Natural History Museum. This song was on the radio and that's when my dad and I both fell in love with this song, my mom as well. After this song, I heard the songs "Loyal" by Chris Brown and "Touchin' Lovin'" by Trey Songz ft. Nicki Minaj on the radio that day (July 5, 2014). I miss when songs like this sound the same. I'm getting pure nostalgia from 2010-2016. I'd do anything to go back to the 2010s and relive these years. They were golden. This song brings back so many memories that I started getting so sad that I can't go back. Enjoy your childhood I hope this song never goes out of style. Wow, it feels like 2014 was only 3 years ago now it's almost a full 10! That's crazy, time went by too fast. June 30, 2014 - June 30, 2024. 10 Years Later! 🥳🥳🥳🥳🥳🥳

It’s wild how A$AP Rocky’s video literally takes you through every stage of an LSD trip. It starts off mellow and chill—super relaxed vibe—then the colors slowly begin to pop, and the music subtly layers in more textures. The girl in the video totally represents the acid itself. She first appears exactly at 1:30, right when you know it’s kicking in, and from that moment on she completely owns his attention while he dives deeper into her.

Different thoughts, different visuals—by the middle of the clip she leads him into this insanely bright, flickering world, and he’s literally overwhelmed by the flood of imagery. Then, at the exact peak of the trip, his mind is racing so fast that he craves something more energetic and intense—cue that massive beat switch in the song. That section lasts about a minute, which you could say feels like an hour in trip time.

Once the high starts to fade, you glide back into that calm, serene state. You’re still wrapped up in her—the acid—getting gentle waves of thoughts or just pure peace. And at the end of the video, it’s like coming down: the colors dim, thoughts return to normal speed, and she, like the acid, slowly dissolves away.

Bottom line: this dude totally gets it, and he’s always talked about acid in a positive way. Major respect.

This song is devastating, if you were to separate the instrumental and the lyrics and examine them separately they completely contrast each other. The melody is calming, peacefully progresses, and would sound like something that would make someone happy. Then you read the lyrics, and it reads as someone who has completely given up on life and this world entirely. Yet the lyrics and the instrumental pair so perfectly. I couldn't imagine any other instrumental expressing the lyrics any better. In a way, it makes sense. When you truly give up, the weight of shame, sadness, anger, and torturous confusion for failing and being looked down upon so many times fades. Now you are left with nothing but you and what ever it is you feel in the present moment now that you have let go of everything. For most, I would assume they would feel nothing, but for Mac, I would like to imagine he felt at peace in his final moments, just like the way the song feels. R.I.P Mac Miller, and thank you for creating the masterpiece that is "Good News".
